question: Constitutional requirement to present the Annual Financial Statement before parliament is given in article _______ of the Constitution of India.
solution:
The correct answer is __**112.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 112** of the Constitution of India deals with the** annual financial **statement, also known as the **Union Budget**.
 
• It states that the **President** shall, at the beginning of every financial year, lay before Parliament the annual financial statement for the year.
 
• The annual financial statement includes the** estimated receipts and expenditure** of the government for the upcoming financial year and is prepared by the **Ministry of Finance.**
 
• The statement is presented in the form of a budget, which is discussed and approved by **both the houses of Parliament** before it comes into effect.
 
• The Constitution of India also mandates that the budget should distinguish between expenditure charged upon the** Consolidated Fund of India **and other expenditure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 12 **of the Constitution deals with the **definition of the State.**
 
• **Article 121** deals with the** restriction** on discussion in Parliament.
 
• **Article 123 **deals with the **power of the President **to promulgate ordinances.
 
• The** Constitution of India** is the supreme law of the country and lays down the framework for the** governance of India.**
 
• It was adopted on** 26th November 1949** and came into effect on** 26th January 1950**, marking the beginning of a new era in the history of India.
 
• The Constitution has **448 articles** in** 25 parts **and **12 schedules**, making it one of the **lengthiest written constitutions** in the world.
 
• It provides for a **federal system of government **with a division of powers between the central and state governments.
 
• The Constitution also guarantees** fundamental rights** to all citizens and outlines the duties of the government towards them.
